data.note:
Reflection on s_3069b9414e – Incorrect: predicted Aurora kinase inhibitors, true simvastatin / Cholesterol-lowering.

Unblinding check: PubChem CID 54454 simvastatin, ChEMBL CHEMBL1064 mechanism HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor [e23], name and BBBC021 structure agree. PubMed confirms class mechanism: Simvastatin. review [PMID:30422514] and Statin Medications. [PMID:28613690] describe statins as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors for cholesterol lowering.

Phenotype re-interpretation: Low dose 0.2-0.6 uM frac_large_nucleus z=6.9,9.9 with multinucleate proxy 4.9 [e5,e2] and high dose 6 uM frac_mitotic_like z=12.1, cell_area z=-10.2, tub_glcm_contrast z=9.6, act_std z=9.1 [e3] mimicked high-dose mitotic / low-dose polyploid pattern. I over-weighted composite-only Microscopist call of Aurora [e19] and biphasic frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.8 / frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.8 [e7,e8] with rising tub_mean rho=+1.0 [e9], tub contrast rho=+1.0 [e13].

Correct weighting: NSC vote was Cholesterol-lowering 2/4, with high-dose wells matching mevinolin/lovastatin – also a statin HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor – at similarity 0.763 (2 uM 0.614) and k-neighbors top 3/10 cholesterol-lowering mean similarity 0.513 vs Eg5 0.337, Actin 0.328 [e6]. Low-dose disagreeing votes had similarity 0.229 to DNA replication and 0.151 to Actin disruptors, i.e. weak/noise, plus field artifact noted (f_ecf681fc22a5 half-empty) in e19. NSC is designed as 1-NN per well majority vote; k-neighbor class counts are expected to be split when many reference treatments exist. I should have kept NSC as prior and required multiple independent high-similarity votes to overturn, not a single vision model.

Why statin looks antimitotic: HMG-CoA inhibition depletes geranylgeranyl/mevalonate → Rho/Rac prenylation defects → actin/tubulin texture changes (act_mean rho +0.8, tub_glcm rho +1.0), reduced cell area/solidity, micronucleation/mitotic-like condensation at cytostatic doses without true Aurora inhibition. No significant cell_count

reflection.text:
This run was unblinded as simvastatin, PubChem CID 54454, ChEMBL CHEMBL1064, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor - truth MoA Cholesterol-lowering PMID 30422514 PMID 28613690 - and my conclusion of Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.53) was incorrect. Verdict correct: false.

What the evidence got right:
The image-based profiling before human re-interpretation pointed to cholesterol-lowering. e6 compare_to_reference_atlas returned NSC vote 2/4 wells Cholesterol-lowering and k-neighbour 3/10 Cholesterol-lowering (tied with Eg5 and Actin at 3/10). That was the strongest atlas signal and it was correct. The high-dose wells that drove that vote were phenotypically extreme and consistent: e3 at 6 uM 297 cells frac_mitotic_like z=+12.1, cell_roundness z=-11.4, cell_area z=-10.2 and e4 at 2 uM 285 cells cell_area z=-8.8, cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-6.5. e9 tub_mean rho=+1.00 (p=0) and e13 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 (p=0) across the 4 acquired wells were also listed as supporting Cholesterol-lowering in hypothesis v1 (0.48) at step 18.

What misled me and why:
I flipped from v1 Cholesterol-lowering 0.48 to v2 Aurora 0.52 after e19 describe_phenotype. That was an error of overweighting weak evidence:

1. Low-dose morphology mis-read as Aurora slippage: e2 at 0.6 uM 61 cells frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0, cell_major_axis +5.3, cell_area +5.0 and e5 at 0.2 uM 245 cells frac_large_nucleus +6.9, frac_multinucleate_proxy +4.9. I interpreted this plus e7 rho=-0.80 (p=0.2) for frac_large_nucleus vs e8 rho=+0.80 (p=0.2) for frac_mitotic_like as biphasic polyploid/multinucleate at low dose -> mitotic arrest at high dose, classic Aurora. In retrospect these dose_response trends were all p=0.2 or p=0.6 (e7,e8,e10,e11,e12,e14,e15,e16,e17) and based on n=4 wells with no replication, so not statistically supported. The only significant trends were e9 and e13 for tubulin, which in e6 context actually favored cholesterol-lowering, not Aurora.

2. Single-observer description: e19 "density lower vs DMSO; 1 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors" was based on 1 observation across 4 fields. I made this decisive in update_hypotheses step 20, moving Aurora to 0.52 and dropping Cholesterol to 0.22 with justification "biphasic dose response and microscopist point consistently to Aurora over cholesterol" and rationale "NSC split 2 cholesterol vs 1 DNA replication,1 actin with low similarity low-dose votes; biphasic dose response and microscopist point consistently to Aurora". I discounted that 2/4 NSC votes is not a split - it was the plurality winner - and that low-dose similarity should not outweigh high-dose concordance without orthogonal markers.

3. Internal inconsistency ignored: e3 cell_roundness z=-11.4 (large negative) is opposite to expected mitotic rounding for Aurora/Eg5 arrest, and e2 had only 61 cells measured vs ~250-300 in other wells, indicating selective cell loss/toxicity at 0.6 uM that was not captured by e15 cell_count rho=-0.40 (p=0.6) trend. I did not interrogate that count drop or the roundness contradiction.

What I missed due to acquisition choices:
I acquired only 4 single-replicate wells (0.2, 0.6, 2, 6 uM) out of 8 doses available (0.006-20 uM) per e1. No 0.006-0.06 uM baseline and no 20 uM max, no rep2, so I could not test reproducibility of the large-nucleus vs mitotic-like switch or distinguish assay noise. The dose_response calculations were therefore underpowered, as shown by p=0.2 for the key fractions.

Literature check afterwards was informative but came after submit: e22/e23 lookup correctly gave HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor with name and BBBC021 structure agreement, and e24 returned 400 hits for simvastatin HMG-CoA mechanism while e25 returned 0 hits for "simvastatin cell cycle arrest mitosis polyploidy actin cytoskeleton". The absence of support for the Aurora/actin narrative should have been a flag before submission.

Next time I would retain the atlas vote as primary when it is 2/4 with extreme high-dose phenotypes, require p<0.05 and replicated dose-response to claim biphasic Aurora-like behavior, and validate with a cholesterol-pathway control rather than relying on a single microscopist annotation of density.

e3/e4 high-dose small-area, high tubulin mean/contrast phenotypes correctly mapped to cholesterol-lowering in v1
e22/e23 unblinding identity check correctly identified HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor
what_was_wrong: v2 upgrade to Aurora 0.52 based on e19 single observation and non-significant rho=-0.80/+0.80 trends p=0.2
Interpretation of e2/e5 large nucleus + multinucleate as Aurora slippage without phospho-H3 or ploidy validation
